resources.string: A backup copies an app\'s APK, its data folders and its expansion files into this app\'s own storage. Every archived file is hashed with SHA-256 right after it is written and read back before the record is saved, so "backed up" means checked, not assumed. Restoring is refused unless every recorded file passes its own hash check. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is encrypted — a key shipped inside the APK is not a secret, and claiming encryption you do not have is worse than not having it.

Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, contacts and call log — with the same verified archive as apps

System data lives in two different places, so it is read two different ways. Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth pairings are system files: root reads them and they are archived with tar, then restored by unpacking. Contacts, call log and messages live behind content providers: they are read as rows and archived as readable JSON, never as a copy of a live database — a copy of a database something is writing to can be half-written. Restoring rows merges: rows that are already there are skipped and counted, and nothing that is not in the backup is deleted. Messages can be read and archived, but Android only lets the default messaging app write them, so restoring them is blocked by the platform — and we say that here instead of offering a button that fails.
Looking for system files and counting provider rows.
No root: file-based categories are out of reach
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings are system files under /data/misc, which this layer cannot read without root. Contacts, call log and messages go through their providers and only need their permissions.
